meta.tagline: The lake city hidden behind the banks: river swims, Dada and chocolate

pills: World league in quality of life
A city centre you can swim through
Birthplace of the Dada art movement

overview.title: Welcome to Zurich
overview.intro: Zurich's fame was written by its banks, but the city's secret lies elsewhere: on summer lunchtimes the suited jump into the Limmat, the old town's steeples hide Chagall windows, and the Dada movement was born on a bar stage here. The industrial district's viaduct arches have turned into design shops, the trams run like clockwork, and the lake poses with its mountain skyline every evening. Zurich looks serious — but keep your swimsuit in your bag: this city knows better than anyone how to strip off and jump in.

local_word.definition: The heart of Zurich's open-air swimming culture: the wooden bathing decks along lake and river. Swimming in the lunch break is a civic tradition — and some badis become bars at night, glasses raised with feet in the water.

rules.title: Take the river swim seriously — and join it
rules.description: The Limmat and the lake are clean enough to swim, and the locals do it daily: use the marked badi areas, learn the exit ladders, and float your belongings in a waterproof bag (a Wickelfisch). Whoever doesn't swim has seen half of Zurich.

rules.title: Respect the quiet hours
rules.description: Swiss order runs through daily life: night and Sunday quiet are taken seriously, and tram phone calls happen at half volume. The rules aren't coldness — they're everyone's comfort; adapt and relax.

rules.title: Manage the prices with strategy
rules.description: Zurich is among the world's most expensive cities: lunch menus, bakeries, supermarket terraces and the free lake-and-river life strike the balance. The fountain water is drinkable everywhere — 1,200 fountains are the city's free bar.

quick_facts.label: Getting around
quick_facts.sub: The ZVV ticket covers them all

quick_facts.label: Signature
quick_facts.sub: City swimming in river and lake

tip.label: The Zurich philosophy
tip.text: The formula for understanding Zurich lives at lunchtime: at 12.00 the bankers jump in the river, at 13.00 the suits go back on. Discipline and pleasure are not rivals here but partners — fit both into the same day.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: Zurich's transport is Swiss watchmaking in public form: the tram web wraps the city, boats run the lake line, and everything works on one ticket.

items.title: Airport to the centre
items.description: The train reaches the main station in 10-15 minutes — ticket from machine or app, punctuality guaranteed. A taxi on this stretch delivers a Swiss price lesson; take the train and skip the lesson.

items.title: The tram — the city's pulse
items.description: The blue-and-white trams serve every quarter to the minute: the ZVV zone ticket covers tram, bus, S-Bahn and boat. The day ticket amortises itself after two rides.

items.title: The lake boats
items.description: The ZSG steamers serve the lake villages on a timetable and take the normal zone ticket: the small circuit (90 min) is the afternoon's most graceful pause. Espresso on deck, the Alpine skyline across the water.

items.title: The old town on foot
items.description: Niederdorf's narrow lanes, the Lindenhof terrace and the riverbanks walk end to end: central Zurich is a city built to foot scale.

items.title: The Uetliberg train
items.description: The S10 climbs the city's home mountain in half an hour: from the summit tower, lake, city and Alps in one panorama. On a normal ZVV ticket — the city's cheapest 'mountain holiday'.

callout.label: Boat tip
callout.text: Time the lake boat for sunset: in the lowering sun the Alps blush and the skyline turns gold. The same ticket, twice the view — read the timetable for the evening run.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Zurich choosing a quarter is choosing a tempo: the old town's fairytale lanes, Zürich West's industrial rhythm, the lakeshore's calm elegance.

local_word.definition: Zurich's 12 districts: a local gives their address as 'I live in Kreis 4'. Each Kreis has a clear character — 1 is history, 4 nightlife, 5 industry-and-design, 8 lakeside grace. Learn the numbers and the city decodes.

items.name: Altstadt / Niederdorf (Kreis 1)
items.description: The historic core between river and lake: steeples, guild squares and Niederdorf's narrow night lanes. Walk to everything — at centre-of-town prices.

items.name: Zürich West (Kreis 5)
items.description: The old factory district's new life: shops in the viaduct arches, Frau Gerold's garden, galleries and towers. Young, industrial and alive — design hotel territory.

items.name: Seefeld (Kreis 8)
items.description: Calm grace on the lake's east shore: badis, the opera and the lake parks in walking distance. A morning run on the shore, an evening glass on the quay — the showcase of quality of life.

items.name: Around Langstrasse (Kreis 4)
items.description: The city's most mixed and lively artery: bars, world kitchens and nightlife. The once-rough quarter is now the young crowd's centre — light sleepers should ask for a back-street room.

items.name: Enge and the west shore (Kreis 2)
items.description: Park museums, the Rote Fabrik culture centre and the lake lidos: minutes to the centre by tram, neighbourhood calm at night. For players of the comfort-and-quiet balance.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Zurich's star season is badi summer; but every season has its stage: a spring street festival, autumn museums, winter light and chocolate.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Sechseläuten Spring
items.subtitle: Spring · The snowman-burning festival, opening terraces
items.description: In mid-April the guilds burn the snowman Böögg at Sechseläuten — the faster his head explodes, the finer the summer will be. The terraces go up, the lakeshore stirs, and the badis open in late May.

callout.label: April tip
callout.text: If you land on Sechseläuten Monday, go to Bellevue: guildsmen on horseback circle the burning Böögg, and the explosion time is a citywide wager. Odd, authentic and very Zurich.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Badi Season
items.subtitle: Summer · River swims, open-air cinema, the Street Parade
items.description: The city moves into the water: lunchtime river swims, badi bars at dusk, open-air cinema on the lakeshore. In August the Street Parade — Europe's biggest techno parade — makes the city unrecognisable for a day.

callout.label: July tip
callout.text: Live one lunchtime like a local: inflate your Wickelfisch, drop into the river at Oberer Letten and drift with the current. A sun deck and coffee at the exit — Zurich's best 'meeting break'.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: Golden Lake Light
items.subtitle: Autumn · Clear days, museum season
items.description: September still allows lake swimming; with October the light turns golden and the museum and concert seasons open. The Uetliberg's fog-sea days begin — city in mist, summit in sun.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: On a foggy October morning ride the S10 up the Uetliberg: sun above the cloud sea, the city invisible below. Enter the Kunsthaus on the way down — a fog day in Zurich is twice as beautiful.

items.label: Winter
items.name: Light and Chocolate
items.subtitle: Winter · Christmas lights, hot chocolate, skiing nearby
items.description: The Bahnhofstrasse light show and the giant Christmas market inside the station crown December; January-February is the calm museum-and-café season. Skiers reach the Alpine resorts within the hour.

callout.label: December tip
callout.text: Drink mulled wine under the Swarovski tree at the Christkindlimarkt inside the main station, then walk beneath Bahnhofstrasse's 'Lucy' lights: the official opening ritual of a Zurich winter.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: Zurich's table is elegant and buttery: the creamy veal classic, the street sausage and the world's most famous chocolate windows live on the same avenue.

local_word.definition: 'At four o'clock': Switzerland's afternoon snack tradition — schoolchildren and workers alike take their zvieri. It is the hour of the bakery-counter crowd; grab a gipfeli and join the custom.

items.name: Zürcher Geschnetzeltes
items.description: Strips of veal in a creamy mushroom sauce with crisp rösti alongside: the classic that carries the city's name. In the guild restaurants the porcelain is heavy and the portion honest — this is Zurich's official plate.

items.name: The Sternen Grill-style bratwurst
items.description: A veal sausage from the coals with a gold bürli roll and fierce mustard: standing Zurich's legend. The queue moves fast and the sausage is eaten by hand — whoever asks for a fork is a stranger.
items.tag: The standing legend · with fierce mustard

items.name: Fondue and the winter pots
items.description: In the cold months the cheese pot appears on every corner, and it's served for visitors even in summer. The traditional mixture with kirsch is dipped with bread — the white-wine escort is the rule.

items.name: Luxemburgerli and the chocolate windows
items.description: Sprüngli's airy mini-macarons, the Luxemburgerli, are the city's sweet signature; the historic chocolatiers' praline counters are museums in themselves. A gift box here is a serious instrument of diplomacy.
items.tag: The sweet signature · from a historic window

items.name: Bakery culture — gipfeli and brezel
items.description: The morning gipfeli (the Swiss croissant) and the buttered brezel: the bakery counters are the address for starting the day and for zvieri. The lunch sandwiches are the budget classic.
items.tag: Morning and zvieri · from the bakery

items.name: Badi bars and local beers
items.description: On summer evenings the badis become bars: feet in the water, a local beer or white wine in the glass. The waterside aperitif culture is Zurich seriousness's most delightful exception.
items.tag: Summer evening · feet in the water

callout.label: Budget tip
callout.text: Three friends manage hunger in Zurich: the lunchtime Tagesmenü boards, the bakery counters and the supermarket terraces with their views. Finish the chocolate gift list at the supermarket shelf — in Switzerland even supermarket chocolate plays in the world league.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone walks the Bahnhofstrasse; these six are Zurich's backstage.

items.name: The Lindenhof terrace
items.description: The linden-shaded square on the site of the Roman fort opens over the old town: giant chess pieces, a fountain and the river view. The centuries-old address of the lunch sandwich and the evening hush.

items.rarity: The stage where Dada was born
items.name: Cabaret Voltaire
items.description: The bar where the Dada movement was born in 1916 still stands: exhibitions, performances and coffee in the historic hall. Art history's most absurd revolution began within these walls — and the place still carries the seriousness of unseriousness.

items.name: The Chagall windows in the Fraumünster
items.description: Chagall's five windows give their deepest blue in morning light: a small church, a large serenity. Enter at opening — the tourist wave arrives at noon.

items.name: Im Viadukt
items.description: Design shops, workshops and a market hall in the stone railway viaduct of Zürich West: industrial heritage's most graceful conversion. The Saturday market hall + a coffee under the arches is the classic.

items.rarity: A night view above the forest
items.name: Sunset on the Uetliberg
items.description: Half an hour up by S10: from the tower, lake, city and the Alpine wall in one panorama. The half hour from sunset to city lights is Zurich's most generous show — and the way down can become a lantern-lit walk.

items.rarity: The wooden baths that turn to bars
items.name: The Frauenbadi and the Rimini night bars
items.description: The historic wooden badis, single-sex by day, open to everyone as bars at night: at the Barfussbar shoes are banned and feet stay in the water. Zurich's most original evening venues — in summer, at water level.

callout.label: River tip
callout.text: The locals' Limmat route: enter at Oberer Letten, drift with the current to Unterer Letten, climb the ladder, sunbathe, repeat. Your waterproof Wickelfisch is both suitcase and float — everything, phone included, swims with you.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Scams are next to nonexistent in Zurich; the traps hide in the price tags and in wrong assumptions.

items.name: Gift hunting on the Bahnhofstrasse
items.description: On the world's most expensive avenue, chocolate and watches sell in 'tourist packaging': the same product is markedly cheaper two streets over.
items.instead: Do the window tour on the Bahnhofstrasse and the buying in the side streets and supermarket aisles. If a luxury watch is the goal, appointments, not haggling, are the culture anyway.

items.name: A taxi for a short hop
items.description: Zurich's taxis rank among the world's costliest, and the tram often does the same route faster.
items.instead: Buy the ZVV day ticket and use the tram-boat-S-Bahn trio; the network runs late into the night too. A taxi makes sense only with a mountain of luggage.

items.name: Sitting down without reading the menu
items.description: An ordinary-looking restaurant's evening main can reach surprise figures: in Zurich the notion of 'average' misleads.
items.instead: Read the window menu before sitting and let the lunch Tagesmenü stand in for dinner. The good news: price transparency is the rule — nothing beyond the printed figure appears, and tipping isn't obligatory.

items.name: Cramming the Alps into one day 'to see Switzerland'
items.description: Whoever sprints from Zurich to three mountain stations in a day spends it on trains; both city and mountains end up half-done.
items.instead: Separate the city day and the mountain day: for the near dose, half a day on the Uetliberg suffices; for the full dose pick one target (Titlis, Rigi or Säntis) and leave early.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: Most of Zurich's best things are free or ticket-priced: the river swim, the Lindenhof, the fountain water, the lakeshore, the Uetliberg. Save the money for one good table and one box of chocolate — the city treats you to the rest.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: A Zurich day from stained glass to river swim

steps.title: The old town morning
steps.description: Say good morning to the city from the Lindenhof terrace; see the Chagall windows in their morning blue at the Fraumünster, breakfast in the Niederdorf lanes.

steps.title: Bahnhofstrasse and the windows
steps.description: Walk the world's most expensive avenue as a window tour; a Luxemburgerli pause at Sprüngli — leave the box decision for the evening.

steps.title: Noon: river or menu
steps.description: In summer, a river swim at Letten + the sun deck; otherwise Geschnetzeltes + rösti at a guild restaurant. Both options are local classics.

steps.title: Exploring Zürich West
steps.description: Tram to Kreis 5: the Im Viadukt arches, Frau Gerold's garden and the galleries — industrial Zurich's new life.

steps.title: Lake boat or badi bar
steps.description: The small lake circuit on the sunset boat, or an aperitif with feet in the water at the Barfussbar: the glasses rise as the Alps blush.

steps.title: Evening in Niederdorf
steps.description: Dinner in the narrow lanes, then a glass at Cabaret Voltaire: an absurd and elegant close to the day between the walls where Dada was born.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: City, lake and summit — the Zurich trilogy

steps.title: Classic Zurich
steps.description: The one-day flow above: Lindenhof, Chagall, Bahnhofstrasse, Zürich West, the lake evening.

steps.title: Art and the quarters
steps.description: The Kunsthaus collection in the morning; world kitchens around Langstrasse at noon; lake time at the Seefeld badis in the afternoon; the opera or a Rote Fabrik concert at night — both extremes are Zurich.

steps.title: The Uetliberg and farewell
steps.description: The S10 up the home mountain: the ridge walk to Felsenegg and the cable car down to Adliswil; one last river swim or the chocolate shop in the afternoon; a farewell dinner over the fondue pot — a kirsch-scented close.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Zurich German sings its own melody; these five open doors on the tram and at the badi alike.

items.meaning: Hello — the greeting of every hour, in city and on mountain
Thank you very much — Switzerland's French-German blend classic
Enjoy your meal — said as the lunch menu lands
Cheers! — valid at the badi bar with feet in the water too
Goodbye — say it leaving a shop and earn a local's smile
